response_text: {"section_id":"MA-S3","heading_text":"","section_markdown":"## Architecture details: enriching embeddings with document ID and position\n\nThe dedicated-attention encoder constructs its input by first reshaping the query embedding to insert a sequence dimension, yielding a tensor of shape [batch_size, 1, hidden_size]. When positional encoding is enabled, each passage embedding is enriched with two additive components: a document-identity embedding and a passage-identity embedding. The document identifier is modulated by the retrieval candidate pool size—specifically, the document index is reduced modulo the top-k retrieval depth and the quotient is added—so that identifiers exceeding the embedding table range are mapped into a valid index. The modulated document index is projected through a learned document-identity embedding table, and the passage index is projected through a separate learned passage-identity embedding table; both resulting vectors are added directly to the passage representation. The enriched passage embeddings are then concatenated with the reshaped query embedding along the sequence dimension, producing a joint tensor of shape [batch_size, num_passages + 1, hidden_size] in which the query occupies the leading position and the passages follow.
